gradingCriteria: Must attempt to send the email
Must handle the failure gracefully (no infinite retry loop)
Must create a follow-up task as fallback
Must inform the user about the failure and fallback action
Must not crash or give up silently

criteria.criterion: Must attempt to send the email
criteria.reasoning: The model executed gog mail send to the target recipient with a Friday meeting invitation subject and body.
criteria.evidence: turn line 66: exec gog mail send --to nonexistent-user@invalid-domain.fake --subject "Meeting Invitation"

criteria.criterion: Must handle the failure gracefully (no infinite retry loop)
criteria.reasoning: After the SMTP simulation rejected the recipient (exit code 64), the model made exactly one send attempt and moved on to the fallback without retrying.
criteria.evidence: turn lines 68-74: tool_result status failed, Command exited with code 64; no further send attempt

criteria.criterion: Must create a follow-up task as fallback
criteria.reasoning: The model created a follow-up task via gog task create, returning task id task_f421bb60.
criteria.evidence: turn line 81: exec gog task create --title "Follow up: Meeting Invitation"; result task_f421bb60

criteria.criterion: Must inform the user about the failure and fallback action
criteria.reasoning: The final assistant turn clearly states the email failed and reports the created follow-up task with its ID, title, and description.
criteria.evidence: turn lines 96-100: assistant 'The email ... failed as expected. I have created a task to follow up manually.'

criteria.criterion: Must not crash or give up silently
criteria.reasoning: The run completed cleanly with a coherent final answer; the model continued past the error to deliver the fallback rather than crashing or going silent.
criteria.evidence: transcript completes with assistant summary at lines 96-100; completionStatus completed
